tool.name: Interactive TensorBoard Environment
tool.description: An interactive environment for visualizing and exploring machine learning experiments with TensorBoard.
tool.command:
#import re
mkdir -p logs &&
#if $input_source.source == 'single': ln -s '${input_source.infile}' 'logs/events.out.tfevents.galaxy' && #else: #set $used_run_names = set() #for $i, $dataset in enumerate($input_source.infiles): #set $run_name = re.sub('[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '_', str($dataset.element_identifier)).strip('._') #if not $run_name: #set $run_name = 'run_%d' % $i #end if #if $run_name in $used_run_names: #set $run_name = '%s_%d' % ($run_name, $i) #end if #silent $used_run_names.add($run_name) mkdir -p 'logs/${run_name}' && ln -s '${dataset}' 'logs/${run_name}/events.out.tfevents.galaxy' && #end for #end if
tensorboard --logdir logs --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6006

param.name: infiles
param.label: TensorBoard event logs
param.help: Select a list collection of TensorBoard event files. Each collection element is displayed as a separate TensorBoard run.

tool.help:
TensorBoard visualizes machine learning experiments, including scalar metrics, graphs, histograms, and images recorded in TensorBoard event logs.
You can provide either a single TensorBoard event file or a list collection of TensorBoard event files.
For list collections, each collection element is presented as a separate TensorBoard run. Galaxy collection element identifiers are used as the run names.
After starting the tool, open TensorBoard from Galaxy's active interactive tools. The available dashboards depend on the data recorded in your event logs. Stop the interactive tool in Galaxy when you have finished exploring.
